text: {"lessons":["Ten periods and modest account fluctuations are too little to judge whether I am outperforming; keep comparing long-run returns with a suitable market benchmark.","Selling at a loss, then buying the same stock again, can reflect changing evidence—but I should define why I enter or exit instead of reacting to losses or recent price moves.","Trading repeatedly without a clear edge risks replacing one position with another at poor times; preserve diversification and sensible position sizes, and trade only when the expected benefit outweighs the costs and risks."]}
